metadata.title: Trust Region Policy Optimization
metadata.authors: John Schulman, Sergey Levine, Philipp Moritz, Michael I. Jordan, Pieter Abbeel

nodes.name: Markov Decision Process (MDP)
nodes.statement: An infinite-horizon discounted MDP is a tuple $(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{A}, P, r, \rho_0, \gamma)$, where $\mathcal{S}$ is a finite state set, $\mathcal{A}$ a finite action set, $P:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{R}$ a transition kernel, $r:\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{R}$ a reward, $\rho_0$ an initial distribution, and $\gamma\in(0,1)$ a discount factor.
nodes.statement_clean: An infinite-horizon discounted MDP with finite state and action sets.

nodes.name: Expected discounted reward $\eta(\pi)$
nodes.statement: $\eta(\pi) = \mathbb{E}_{s_0,a_0,\dots}\!\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^t r(s_t)\right]$ where $s_0\sim\rho_0$, $a_t\sim\pi(a_t\mid s_t)$, $s_{t+1}\sim P(\cdot\mid s_t,a_t)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected discounted return of a stochastic policy $\pi$.

nodes.name: State-action value, value, and advantage functions
nodes.statement: $Q_\pi(s_t,a_t)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_{l=0}^\infty\gamma^l r(s_{t+l})\right]$; $V_\pi(s_t)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_{l=0}^\infty\gamma^l r(s_{t+l})\right]$; $A_\pi(s,a)=Q_\pi(s,a)-V_\pi(s)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard $Q$, $V$, and advantage functions for policy $\pi$.

nodes.name: Discounted state-visitation frequency $\rho_\pi$
nodes.statement: $\rho_\pi(s) = P(s_0=s) + \gamma P(s_1=s) + \gamma^2 P(s_2=s) + \dots$, with $s_0\sim\rho_0$ and actions chosen according to $\pi$.

nodes.name: Local surrogate $L_\pi(\tilde\pi)$
nodes.statement: $L_\pi(\tilde\pi)=\eta(\pi)+\sum_s \rho_\pi(s)\sum_a \tilde\pi(a\mid s)A_\pi(s,a)$. Uses $\rho_\pi$ instead of $\rho_{\tilde\pi}$, ignoring visitation changes due to the policy update.

nodes.name: Total variation divergence $D_{TV}$ and $D^{max}_{TV}$
nodes.statement: $D_{TV}(p\,\|\,q)=\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_i |p_i-q_i|$ for discrete $p,q$; $D^{max}_{TV}(\pi,\tilde\pi)=\max_s D_{TV}(\pi(\cdot\mid s)\,\|\,\tilde\pi(\cdot\mid s))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Total variation distance and its state-wise maximum between two policies.

nodes.name: Maximum and average KL divergence $D^{max}_{KL}$, $\bar D_{KL}^{\rho}$
nodes.statement: $D^{max}_{KL}(\pi,\tilde\pi)=\max_s D_{KL}(\pi(\cdot\mid s)\,\|\,\tilde\pi(\cdot\mid s))$; $\bar D_{KL}^{\rho}(\theta_1,\theta_2)=\mathbb{E}_{s\sim\rho}\!\left[D_{KL}(\pi_{\theta_1}(\cdot\mid s)\,\|\,\pi_{\theta_2}(\cdot\mid s))\right]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Worst-case (over states) and $\rho$-weighted average KL divergence between two policies.

nodes.name: $\alpha$-coupled policy pair
nodes.section: Appendix A (Proof of Policy Improvement Bound)
nodes.statement: $(\pi,\tilde\pi)$ is an $\alpha$-coupled policy pair if there is a joint distribution over $(a,\tilde a)\mid s$ with marginals $\pi(\cdot\mid s)$ and $\tilde\pi(\cdot\mid s)$ such that $P(a\neq\tilde a\mid s)\le\alpha$ for every $s$.
nodes.statement_clean: Joint distribution coupling two policies so they disagree with probability at most $\alpha$ in every state.

nodes.name: Mean advantage $\bar A(s)$
nodes.statement: $\bar A(s)=\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\tilde\pi(\cdot\mid s)}[A_\pi(s,a)]$ — expected advantage of $\tilde\pi$ over $\pi$ at state $s$.

nodes.name: Advantage identity for policy returns
nodes.statement: $\eta(\tilde\pi)=\eta(\pi)+\mathbb{E}_{s_0,a_0,\dots\sim\tilde\pi}\!\left[\sum_{t=0}^\infty \gamma^t A_\pi(s_t,a_t)\right]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Identity expressing the return of $\tilde\pi$ in terms of cumulative advantages of $\tilde\pi$ over $\pi$.

nodes.name: State-form rewrite of advantage identity
nodes.statement: $\eta(\tilde\pi)=\eta(\pi)+\sum_s \rho_{\tilde\pi}(s)\sum_a \tilde\pi(a\mid s) A_\pi(s,a)$.

nodes.name: Kakade--Langford lower bound for conservative policy iteration
nodes.statement: $\eta(\pi_{\mathrm{new}}) \ge L_{\pi_{\mathrm{old}}}(\pi_{\mathrm{new}}) - \frac{2\epsilon\gamma}{(1-\gamma)^2}\alpha^2$ with $\epsilon=\max_s |\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi'(a\mid s)}A_\pi(s,a)|$.
nodes.statement_clean: Original policy improvement bound for mixture (CPI) policies.

nodes.name: KL-divergence policy improvement bound
nodes.statement: $\eta(\tilde\pi) \ge L_\pi(\tilde\pi) - C\, D^{max}_{KL}(\pi,\tilde\pi)$, with $C=\frac{4\epsilon\gamma}{(1-\gamma)^2}$.

nodes.name: Policy improvement bound (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha=D^{max}_{TV}(\pi_{\mathrm{old}},\pi_{\mathrm{new}})$. Then $\eta(\pi_{\mathrm{new}}) \ge L_{\pi_{\mathrm{old}}}(\pi_{\mathrm{new}}) - \frac{4\epsilon\gamma}{(1-\gamma)^2}\alpha^2$ where $\epsilon=\max_{s,a}|A_\pi(s,a)|$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalizes the Kakade--Langford bound from mixture policies to arbitrary stochastic policies, using total variation distance.
assumptions: $\pi_{\mathrm{old}}, \pi_{\mathrm{new}}$ are stochastic policies on a discounted MDP

nodes.name: Per-timestep advantage decomposition (improvelemma)
nodes.statement: Given two policies $\pi,\tilde\pi$: $\eta(\tilde\pi)=\eta(\pi)+\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\tilde\pi}\!\left[\sum_{t=0}^\infty \gamma^t A_\pi(s_t,a_t)\right]$.
assumptions: $\pi,\tilde\pi$ are policies on a discounted MDP

nodes.name: Bound on mean advantage under coupled policies
nodes.statement: If $(\pi,\tilde\pi)$ is an $\alpha$-coupled policy pair, then for all $s$: $|\bar A(s)| \le 2\alpha\,\max_{s,a}|A_\pi(s,a)|$.

nodes.name: Bound on state-distribution shift in mean advantage (advbound)
nodes.statement: Let $(\pi,\tilde\pi)$ be an $\alpha$-coupled policy pair. Then $|\mathbb{E}_{s_t\sim\tilde\pi}\bar A(s_t) - \mathbb{E}_{s_t\sim\pi}\bar A(s_t)| \le 2\alpha\max_s\bar A(s) \le 4\alpha(1-(1-\alpha)^t)\max_{s,a}|A_\pi(s,a)|$.

nodes.name: Pinsker / TV-KL inequality
nodes.statement: For any distributions $p,q$: $D_{TV}(p\,\|\,q)^2 \le D_{KL}(p\,\|\,q)$.
nodes.origin_citation: Pollard, A User's Guide to Measure Theoretic Probability, Ch. 3

nodes.name: Coupling characterization of total variation
nodes.statement: If $D_{TV}(p_X,p_Y)=\alpha$ then there exists a joint distribution $(X,Y)$ with marginals $p_X, p_Y$ and $P(X=Y)\ge 1-\alpha$.
assumptions: $p_X, p_Y$ are distributions on a common space
nodes.origin_citation: Levin, Peres, Wilmer, Markov Chains and Mixing Times, Prop. 4.7

nodes.name: Coupling proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: By coupling $\pi,\tilde\pi$ with disagreement probability $\le\alpha$, decomposing the advantage expectation by whether disagreement has occurred before time $t$, summing the per-timestep error bound, and converting $\alpha$ via the TV-coupling correspondence.

nodes.name: Perturbation theory proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Write $G=(1-\gamma P_\pi)^{-1}$ and $\tilde G=(1-\gamma P_{\tilde\pi})^{-1}$, expand $\tilde G - G$ to second order in $\Delta=P_{\tilde\pi}-P_\pi$, identify the first-order term with $L_\pi(\tilde\pi)-L_\pi(\pi)$, and bound the $O(\Delta^2)$ remainder using $\ell_1$ operator norms with $\|\Delta\|_1=2\alpha$.

nodes.name: Apply per-timestep advantage decomposition
nodes.statement: Invoke Lemma 1 to write $\eta(\tilde\pi)-\eta(\pi)=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\tilde\pi}[\sum_t\gamma^t A_\pi(s_t,a_t)]$, and rewrite both $\eta(\tilde\pi)$ and $L_\pi(\tilde\pi)$ in terms of $\bar A(s_t)$ under trajectory measures $\tilde\pi$ and $\pi$.

nodes.name: Couple policies and split by disagreement
nodes.statement: For an $\alpha$-coupled pair, decompose $\mathbb{E}_{s_t\sim\tilde\pi}[\bar A(s_t)]$ and $\mathbb{E}_{s_t\sim\pi}[\bar A(s_t)]$ over the event $n_t=0$ (no disagreement before $t$); the $n_t=0$ contributions match and cancel.

nodes.name: Bound disagreement probability and conditional advantage gap
nodes.statement: Use $P(n_t>0)\le 1-(1-\alpha)^t$ together with $|\bar A(s)|\le 2\alpha\,\epsilon$ (Lemma 2) to obtain $|\mathbb{E}_{s_t\sim\tilde\pi}\bar A(s_t)-\mathbb{E}_{s_t\sim\pi}\bar A(s_t)|\le 4\alpha(1-(1-\alpha)^t)\epsilon$ (Lemma 3).

nodes.name: Sum over time and simplify
nodes.statement: Sum the per-timestep bound with weight $\gamma^t$: $|\eta(\tilde\pi)-L_\pi(\tilde\pi)|\le 4\epsilon\alpha\big(\frac{1}{1-\gamma}-\frac{1}{1-\gamma(1-\alpha)}\big)=\frac{4\alpha^2\gamma\epsilon}{(1-\gamma)(1-\gamma(1-\alpha))}\le\frac{4\alpha^2\gamma\epsilon}{(1-\gamma)^2}$.

nodes.name: Convert $\alpha$ from coupling to TV divergence
nodes.statement: By the TV-coupling correspondence (Theorem 3 cited), if $D^{max}_{TV}(\pi,\tilde\pi)\le\alpha$, then an $\alpha$-coupled pair with the right marginals exists; substitute $\alpha=D^{max}_{TV}$ to conclude Theorem 1.

nodes.name: Set up resolvent operators
nodes.statement: Define $G=(1-\gamma P_\pi)^{-1}=\sum_k(\gamma P_\pi)^k$ and $\tilde G=(1-\gamma P_{\tilde\pi})^{-1}$, so $\eta(\pi)=rG\rho_0$ and $\eta(\tilde\pi)=r\tilde G\rho_0$. Set $\Delta=P_{\tilde\pi}-P_\pi$.

nodes.name: Expand $\tilde G - G$ to second order in $\Delta$
nodes.statement: From $G^{-1}-\tilde G^{-1}=\gamma\Delta$ derive $\tilde G=G+\gamma G\Delta\tilde G=G+\gamma G\Delta G+\gamma^2 G\Delta G\Delta\tilde G$, hence $\eta(\tilde\pi)-\eta(\pi)=\gamma rG\Delta G\rho_0+\gamma^2 rG\Delta G\Delta\tilde G\rho_0$.

nodes.name: Identify the leading term with $L_\pi(\tilde\pi)-L_\pi(\pi)$
nodes.statement: Using $rG=v$ and $G\rho_0=\rho_\pi$, compute $\gamma v\Delta\rho_\pi$ and verify it equals $L_\pi(\tilde\pi)-L_\pi(\pi)$ via direct expansion of $L_\pi$.

nodes.name: Bound the $O(\Delta^2)$ remainder
nodes.statement: Show $\|\gamma rG\Delta\|_\infty=\|\gamma v\Delta\|_\infty\le 2\alpha\epsilon$ and $\|G\Delta\tilde G\rho\|_1\le \|G\|_1\|\Delta\|_1\|\tilde G\|_1=2\alpha/(1-\gamma)^2$, giving $|\gamma^2 rG\Delta G\Delta\tilde G\rho|\le 4\gamma\epsilon\alpha^2/(1-\gamma)^2$, which yields Theorem 1.

nodes.name: TRPO trust-region policy optimization problem
nodes.statement: $\maximize_\theta L_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(\theta)$ subject to $\bar D^{\rho_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}}_{KL}(\theta_{\mathrm{old}},\theta) \le \delta$.
nodes.statement_clean: Maximize the surrogate objective subject to a bound on the average KL divergence to the previous policy.

nodes.name: Max-KL constrained policy optimization
nodes.statement: $\maximize_\theta L_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(\theta)$ subject to $D^{max}_{KL}(\theta_{\mathrm{old}},\theta)\le\delta$.
nodes.statement_clean: Theoretically motivated trust-region problem with a per-state KL bound; impractical due to many constraints.

nodes.name: Sample-based importance-sampled TRPO subproblem
nodes.statement: $\maximize_\theta\,\mathbb{E}_{s\sim\rho_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}},a\sim q}\!\left[\frac{\pi_\theta(a\mid s)}{q(a\mid s)} Q_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(s,a)\right]$ subject to $\mathbb{E}_{s\sim\rho_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}}[D_{KL}(\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(\cdot\mid s)\,\|\,\pi_\theta(\cdot\mid s))]\le\delta$.
nodes.statement_clean: Importance-sampling expectation form of the TRPO update used by Monte Carlo estimation.

nodes.name: Policy iteration with KL-penalty (Algorithm 1)
nodes.statement: Iteratively maximize $M_i(\pi)=L_{\pi_i}(\pi)-C\, D^{max}_{KL}(\pi_i,\pi)$ at each step; this MM scheme guarantees a non-decreasing sequence $\eta(\pi_0)\le\eta(\pi_1)\le\dots$.

nodes.name: Initialize
nodes.statement: Set $\pi_0$ to an initial policy.

nodes.name: Outer loop over iterations
nodes.statement: For $i=0,1,2,\dots$ until convergence: compute advantages and update.

nodes.name: Compute advantages
nodes.statement: Compute all advantage values $A_{\pi_i}(s,a)$ under the current policy.

nodes.name: Solve the penalized subproblem
nodes.statement: Set $\pi_{i+1}=\arg\max_\pi\big[L_{\pi_i}(\pi)-C\,D^{max}_{KL}(\pi_i,\pi)\big]$ with $C=4\epsilon\gamma/(1-\gamma)^2$.

nodes.name: Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO)
nodes.statement: Practical policy update: collect samples (single-path or vine), build estimated objective and KL constraint, then approximately solve the constrained subproblem via conjugate gradient and a line search.
output: Updated parameters $\theta_{\mathrm{new}}$ satisfying $\bar D^{\rho_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}}_{KL}(\theta_{\mathrm{old}},\theta_{\mathrm{new}})\le\delta$ with improved estimated $L_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}$

nodes.name: Sample trajectories (single-path or vine)
nodes.statement: Use the single-path or vine procedure to collect a set of state-action pairs together with Monte Carlo estimates of their $Q$-values $\hat Q_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(s,a)$.

nodes.name: Build empirical objective and constraint
nodes.statement: By averaging over samples, construct the estimated importance-sampled objective and the average-KL constraint of $L_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}$ and $\bar D^{\rho_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}}_{KL}$ as in problem ProbP243.3.

nodes.name: Compute search direction by conjugate gradient
nodes.statement: Approximately solve $A x = g$ where $A$ is the Fisher information matrix (Hessian of $\bar D_{KL}$) and $g$ is the policy-gradient estimate, using conjugate gradient with $k\approx 10$ Hessian-vector products.

nodes.name: Compute maximal step length
nodes.statement: Take $\beta=\sqrt{2\delta/(s^T A s)}$ so that the quadratic approximation $\tfrac{1}{2}\beta^2 s^T A s = \delta$ matches the KL bound.

nodes.name: Backtracking line search
nodes.statement: Starting from $\beta$, exponentially shrink the step size until both $L_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}$ improves and the nonlinear KL constraint $\bar D_{KL}\le\delta$ is satisfied; set $\theta_{\mathrm{new}}=\theta_{\mathrm{old}}+\beta s$.

nodes.name: Repeat
nodes.statement: Set $\theta_{\mathrm{old}}\leftarrow\theta_{\mathrm{new}}$ and repeat from sampling.

nodes.name: Single-path sampling procedure
nodes.statement: Sample $s_0\sim\rho_0$, simulate $\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}$ for $T$ steps to produce a trajectory; use $q(a\mid s)=\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(a\mid s)$ and estimate $\hat Q_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(s_t,a_t)$ as the discounted sum of future rewards.

nodes.name: Vine sampling procedure
nodes.statement: Sample trunk trajectories from $\pi_{\theta_i}$, choose a rollout set of $N$ states, draw $K$ actions per state from $q(\cdot\mid s_n)$, and estimate $\hat Q_{\theta_i}(s_n,a_{n,k})$ via short rollouts using common random numbers; combine via the (self-normalized) importance-sampling estimator.
output: Per-state surrogate $L_n(\theta)$ and the assembled estimator for $L_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}$

nodes.name: Conservative Policy Iteration (CPI)
nodes.statement: Update via the mixture $\pi_{\mathrm{new}}(a\mid s)=(1-\alpha)\pi_{\mathrm{old}}(a\mid s)+\alpha\pi'(a\mid s)$ where $\pi'=\arg\max_{\pi'} L_{\pi_{\mathrm{old}}}(\pi')$.

nodes.name: Natural Policy Gradient
nodes.statement: Special case of TRPO with linear approximation to $L$ and quadratic approximation to $\bar D_{KL}$: $\theta_{\mathrm{new}}=\theta_{\mathrm{old}}+\frac{1}{\lambda}A(\theta_{\mathrm{old}})^{-1}\nabla_\theta L|_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}$, where $A$ is the Fisher information matrix.

nodes.name: Monotonic improvement of Algorithm 1 (MM perspective)
nodes.statement: Defining $M_i(\pi)=L_{\pi_i}(\pi)-C\,D^{max}_{KL}(\pi_i,\pi)$, $\eta(\pi_{i+1})-\eta(\pi_i)\ge M_i(\pi_{i+1})-M_i(\pi_i)$, so maximizing $M_i$ at each step monotonically improves $\eta$ — a minorization-maximization scheme.

nodes.name: Average-KL relaxation in practice
nodes.statement: Replacing the per-state $D^{max}_{KL}\le\delta$ constraint with the average $\bar D^{\rho}_{KL}\le\delta$ is a heuristic relaxation; experiments show similar empirical behavior to the max-KL form.

nodes.name: Analytic Fisher information matrix vs. empirical FIM
nodes.statement: $A_{ij}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_n\partial_{\theta_i}\partial_{\theta_j} D_{KL}(\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(\cdot\mid s_n)\,\|\,\pi_\theta(\cdot\mid s_n))$ is preferred over the gradient-covariance estimate; it integrates over actions analytically and avoids storing dense Hessians.

nodes.name: Fisher--vector product via $J^T M J$
nodes.statement: Writing the policy as $\pi_\theta=p(\cdot\mid \mu_\theta(x))$, the Fisher information factors as $J^T M J$ where $J=\partial \mu/\partial\theta$ and $M$ is the Fisher of the distribution in $\mu$; the Fisher--vector product $y\mapsto J^T M J y$ uses standard back-prop and a closed-form $M$.

nodes.name: Simulated robotic locomotion (swimmer, hopper, walker)
nodes.statement: TRPO (single-path and vine) trained Gaussian neural-network policies (state dims 10, 12, 18; up to 8206 parameters) on three MuJoCo locomotion tasks with $\delta=0.01$ and $\gamma=0.99$, learning swimming, hopping and walking gaits and outperforming CEM, CMA, natural-gradient and empirical-FIM baselines.

nodes.name: Atari games from raw images
nodes.statement: TRPO trained convolutional policies with $\sim$33{,}500 parameters on seven Atari games, with single-path and vine variants achieving competitive scores against deep $Q$-learning and UCC-I baselines.

nodes.name: Cartpole baseline
nodes.statement: Classical cart-pole balancing problem with a six-parameter linear policy serves as a baseline where the max-KL variant (Equation eq:maxklconst) remains tractable, allowing comparison against the average-KL form used by TRPO.
